verses.text: Samuel died, and all Israel gathered to mourn him. They buried him at his home in Ramah. Then David went down to the wilderness of Paran.
There was a wealthy man from Maon who owned property in Carmel. He had three thousand sheep and a thousand goats, and he was shearing his sheep in Carmel.
His name was Nabal, and his wife's name was Abigail. She was intelligent and beautiful, but he was harsh and acted badly. He belonged to Caleb's family.
While David was in the wilderness, he heard that Nabal was shearing his sheep.
David sent ten young men. He told them, “Go up to Carmel, find Nabal, and greet him for me.
Tell him, ‘Long life to you! May you, your family, and all that you have enjoy peace.
I hear it's shearing time. Your shepherds were with us, and we never harmed them. Nothing of theirs went missing the whole time they were at Carmel.
Ask your young men, and they'll tell you. Please welcome my men, because we've come on a day of celebration. Give whatever you can spare to your servants and to your son David.’”
David's men arrived, delivered his whole message to Nabal, and waited.
Nabal answered, “Who's David? Who's this son of Jesse? There are plenty of servants running away from their masters these days.
Why should I take my bread, my water, and the meat I prepared for my shearers and give it to strangers from who knows where?”
David's men turned around and went back to tell him everything Nabal had said.
David ordered his men to put on their swords. They did, and David put on his own sword. About four hundred followed David, while two hundred stayed with the supplies.
Meanwhile, one of Nabal's young servants told Abigail, “David sent messengers out of the wilderness to greet our master, and he insulted them.
Those men treated us well. They never harmed us, and nothing went missing the whole time we were with them in the fields.
They were like a wall around us day and night while we looked after the sheep near them.
Think carefully about what to do. Disaster is coming for our master and his whole household. He's so difficult that nobody can even talk to him.”
Abigail hurried and loaded donkeys with two hundred loaves, two containers of wine, five dressed sheep, five measures of roasted grain, a hundred clusters of raisins, and two hundred fig cakes.
She told her servants, “Go on ahead. I'll follow you.” She said nothing to her husband Nabal.
As she rode down along the hidden side of the mountain, David and his men came down toward her, and she met them.
David had been saying, “I guarded everything this man owned in the wilderness, and nothing of his went missing. It was all for nothing. He paid me back with evil for the good I did.
May God deal severely with David's enemies if I leave even one of Nabal's men alive by morning.”
As soon as Abigail saw David, she got off her donkey, fell facedown in front of him, and bowed to the ground.
At his feet she said, “My lord, let the blame fall on me. Please give me a chance to speak and hear what I have to say.
Please don't pay attention to that worthless man Nabal. He lives up to his name. His name means ‘fool,’ and foolishness follows him. I didn't see the young men you sent.

My lord, as surely as the LORD lives and as surely as you live, the LORD has kept you from bloodshed and from taking revenge with your own hands. May your enemies and everyone who wants to harm you end up like Nabal.
Please give this gift I've brought you to the young men who follow you.
Please forgive me. The LORD will establish a lasting family for you, my lord, because you fight his battles. May no wrongdoing be found in you all your life.
Even if someone comes after you to take your life, the LORD your God will keep you safe in the bundle of the living. He'll sling away the lives of your enemies like stones from a sling.
When the LORD has done all the good he promised you and made you ruler over Israel,
you won't have to live with the grief or guilt of shedding innocent blood or taking revenge yourself. When the LORD has been good to you, remember me.”
David told Abigail, “Praise the LORD, the God of Israel, who sent you to meet me today!
Bless you for your good judgment. You've kept me from bloodshed today and stopped me from taking revenge with my own hands.
As surely as the LORD, the God of Israel, lives, he kept me from harming you. If you hadn't come quickly to meet me, not one of Nabal's men would have been left alive by morning.”
David took the gift she'd brought and told her, “Go home in peace. I've listened to you and granted your request.”
When Abigail got home, Nabal was holding a feast fit for a king. He was in high spirits and very drunk, so she told him nothing until morning.
In the morning, after Nabal sobered up, Abigail told him what had happened. His heart failed him, and he became like a stone.
About ten days later the LORD struck Nabal, and he died.

When David heard Nabal was dead, he said, “Praise the LORD! He took up my case after Nabal insulted me and kept me from doing wrong. The LORD brought Nabal's wrongdoing back on his own head.” Then David sent word to Abigail asking her to marry him.
David's servants came to Abigail at Carmel and told her, “David sent us to bring you to him as his wife.”
She rose, bowed with her face to the ground, and said, “I'm ready to serve, even to wash the feet of my lord's servants.”
Abigail quickly got up and rode off on a donkey with her five attendants. She went with David's messengers and became his wife.
David had also married Ahinoam from Jezreel, so both women were his wives.
Saul had given his daughter Michal, David's wife, to Palti son of Laish, from Gallim.
